title: Contextual golden-proxy regression sentry for cost-driven batching/caching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, production-safe regression sentinel that catches subtle quality degradations introduced by automated batching/caching recommendations (autotune) before they affect customers. We introduce the concept of 'golden-proxies' — compact, context-parameterized prompt/response probes derived from high-confidence golden prompts and augmented to cover realistic distributional context shifts (prefixes, slot values, conversation turns). The sentinel will run both offline and in shadow mode during canaries and will produce probabilistic alerts backed by statistical tests and human-in-the-loop escalation thresholds.

Why: Current autotune flows reduce token cost but occasionally shift output behavior in small ways (formatting, verbosity, instruction-following). Existing golden-prompt checks are brittle to contextual differences and miss regressions introduced only under specific context shapes. Golden-proxies increase sensitivity while staying low-cost to evaluate.

Design summary:
- Golden-proxy corpus: 400 probes organized by workload slice (short completion, long reasoning, instruction-follow, structured output, multi-turn chat). Each probe is parameterized with 5 context templates (user metadata, prior-turn noise, varying sequence lengths) to emulate realistic prefixes. Corpus stored in Drive/Confluence with provenance.
- Metrics: token-level cost delta, response-quality signals (semantic-similarity via embed cosine, instruction-following binary score, structured-output schema match rate, hallucination score using knowledge-check queries), and behavioral stability fingerprint (n-gram/levenshtein change).
- Statistical acceptance: For any proposed cost config change we compute stratified A/B comparisons between control and treated groups using bootstrap confidence intervals and two-sided permutation tests. Acceptance window requires: no metric regressions beyond absolute thresholds and p-value > 0.01 for harmful regressions. We also compute Bayesian posterior probability of degradation; auto-apply is allowed only if posterior probability of harm < 0.05 and effect size < pre-registered delta.
- Shadow canary flow: New suggested batching/cache config first runs in shadow across a 1% traffic slice with synchronous logging (no user-visible changes). The sentinel evaluates golden-proxy responses plus sampled production traces over a 24-hour rolling window. If any probe crosses hard thresholds (e.g., instruction-following drop >5% absolute OR hallucination increase >2% absolute with p<0.01), we block rollout and create an incident with automated repro bundle.
- Automated rollback: If a config was applied and an alert fires in the first 3 hours that meets auto-rollback criteria (statistically significant degradation and confirmed by at least one secondary metric), the system triggers an automated rollback and opens ENG runbook with required human review.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Data engineering: curate golden-proxy corpus and tagging schema (owner: MLE team). Deliverable: Drive folder + manifest CSV.
2) Offline evaluator: implement batch runner that computes all metrics on historical traces and produces report with CI.
3) Shadow deployer: instrumentation to run probe set in shadow for candidate configs; integrate with existing canary orchestrator.
4) Threshold manager: UI + config store for per-project acceptance thresholds and escalation rules (console-2026.03).
5) Rollback automation: integrate with rollout engine to support immediate rollback and incident creation.

Tradeoffs and open questions:
- Sensitivity vs false positives: tighter thresholds catch more regressions but increase human review load. We'll maintain adaptive thresholds per-team based on historical volatility.
- Corpus representativeness: golden-proxies are a compromise between breadth and evaluation cost. We will expand probes based on customer-facing incident logs.
- Metric selection: embed cosine is robust to lexical drift but can miss instruction-following regressions; hybrid metrics mitigate this but complicate acceptance logic.

Success criteria:
- Detect >=90% of synthetic regressions introduced by known cost-optimization patches in internal sim runs.
- Reduce customer-facing regression incidents attributed to autotune by 80% in the next quarter.

Artifacts: design doc (Confluence), golden-proxy corpus (Drive), prototype evaluator (GitHub PR), dashboard (Console release runtime-1.25).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Spike complete: parameterized probe idea validated on small LLaMA-derived model. Found that 3 context templates per probe detect 60% more regressions than single golden prompts (prototype dataset of 120 probes). Owner: Marco.

2026-03-05 - Design review notes from PM Lena Cho: suggested adding structured-output schema checks and a secondary human-audit gate for high-business-cost routes. Action: add schema match metric and human audit threshold config.

2026-03-07 - Eng review (SRE): asked for low-overhead telemetry approach. Decided to reuse existing tracing hooks and store probe responses in the ephemeral canary buffer (30 day retention). Action: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345 (shadow-probe-hook).

2026-03-09 - Prototype results: shadow run on dev cluster for candidate config reduced token spend by 12% and produced 6 probe failures (instruction-follow drops) concentrated in multi-turn chat templates. Next: tune batch sizes for those slices and re-run offline sims.
2026-03-11 - Data note from MLE (Sofia Ramos): need 3x more labeled examples for hallucination checks. Added task to build small labeled set from production traces (sampling approval requested).
2026-03-12 - PM decision: use two-tier thresholds (soft warning -> human audit, hard threshold -> block/rollback). Implement escalation flow in console-2026.03 release.

2026-03-13 - Blocker: access to customer-specific prompt templates for enterprise customers is gated. Solution: build synthetic templates based on documented schemas; long-term: request opt-in telemetry. Raised to product and legal for review.

2026-03-14 - Now: integrating evaluator into CI pipeline for runtime-1.25; landed initial PR for offline scorer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-suite/pull/78. Next: wire shadow canary and create dashboard widgets (cost delta, probe pass rate, posterior risk).
